overall: The AG found the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by entering executive session under Purpose 6 for an unrelated party's land deal; the non-member advisor's presence was not a violation. Compliance and minutes release ordered.

allegations.summary: Commission entered executive session under Purpose 6 (real property) for a potential collaboration with an entity buying land, though the Commission was not a party to that purchase.
allegations.key_passage: By meeting in executive session for an improper purpose, the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: A non-member volunteer Commission advisor was permitted to attend the August 6, 2024 executive session, which the complainant alleged was improper.
allegations.key_passage: Had the executive session been convened for a proper purpose, this individual's presence would have been proper.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Publicly release the August 6, 2024, executive session minutes.
remedy_passage: We order the Commission's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that future similar violations may be viewed as evidence of intent to violate the law. We further order the Commission to publicly release the August 6, 2024, executive session minutes.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
